name: Clometacin

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in France, first in 1987 — for liver harm

similar.name: Indomethacin
problems: Carries a boxed warning in United States — for nerve and brain harm, stomach and gut problems and heart harm

similar.name: Clofibrate
problems: Pulled from the market in Israel and 2 other countries, first in 1979 — for blood vessel problems and cancer risk

summary: Clometacin was removed from the market in France starting in 1987 due to liver damage [3]. A small computer program, rather than tests done on humans, calculated a high risk score of 81 for the liver and a low risk score of 28 for the heart [M]. A similar medicine called Indomethacin has a severe warning label in the United States for heart injury, stomach or gut injury, and nervous system damage [4]. Another related drug, Clofibrate, was taken off the market in Israel and two other countries because of blood vessel damage and cancer risks [5].
